drift_findings.rationale: The phase design's pinned Section 1.2/5.5 procedure — reinstall the repository skills first, dogfood the semantic surface on the installed build, and reinstall again before the milestone commit — was not performed; the user forbade installs mid-phase and the implementation substituted a new dev-mode mechanism (scripts/dev-mcp-launcher.sh plus a rewritten .mcp.json routing through it) that the approved design does not describe. Section 5.2 scoped src/mcp/handlers/session.ts's staged-config copy for deletion; it was retained under the design's own stranded-consumer allowance. Most significantly, the change set is based on a merge of origin/main (base_commit 54d60e9) that brings in baseline-adoption gate/overlay machinery, and it adds two kernel behavior changes the design's 'no new action kind, substep code, capability, or durable state shape' boundary did not contemplate: the absence-aware projection union in reconciliation discovery and the unrestorable-missing produce re-entry route in deriveNextAction. Each departure is recorded in phases/4/impl-notes.md and, for the routing change, in docs/state/DURABLE-STATE.md, and none contradicts the design's success criteria — the merge was in fact needed for criterion 5 (existing durable tasks must project and operate) to hold for this very task, and the advertised two-tool boundary, gate authority model, and retirement set match the approved design. The drift is material because the approved phase-design text still describes an install-based self-cutover, a session.ts deletion, and a scope that excludes the merged and kernel-level behavior now shipping, so a reader of the design alone would not anticipate the delivered surface.

rule_findings.rationale: Implementation followed an approved phase design, and every departure is explicitly recorded rather than silent: the impl-notes enumerate each deviation with its cause, docs/state/DURABLE-STATE.md was updated in the same change for the routing fix, and the design's own risk section pre-authorizes keeping a module that turns out to have a live consumer provided the deviation is recorded in impl notes (the session.ts case). The parent-design Section 3.5 correction was verified already present in the committed bytes. The architectural invariants the design pins are intact in the snapshot: the advertised surface is exactly the semantic pair (src/contracts/tool-names.ts:18), no new durable state shape was added (the new reconciliation fields are discovery-only annotations, src/state/reconciliation.ts:44-53), and recovery routing reuses the existing run-step action kind. The whole change set is re-entering the applicable review boundary here before any dependent work advances, and this is the terminal planned phase, so no successor has proceeded on undisclosed deviations. The unamended phase-design text for the merge- and kernel-derived scope is reported as drift below rather than as a rule breach.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: The subject is phase-4 implementation output produced under the approved phases/4/design.md, and its impl-notes declare several departures from that design: the pinned §1.2/§5.5 self-cutover reinstall was skipped, src/mcp/handlers/session.ts kept a fallback the design scheduled for deletion, an origin/main merge (base_commit 54d60e9) absorbed baseline-adoption machinery, and two kernel recovery fixes (absence-aware projection union in src/state/reconciliation-discovery.ts:213-248, unrestorable-missing routing in src/state/next-action.ts:288-317) landed beyond the design's stated scope.

rule_findings.rationale: Every advancement remains bound to an explicit human record for the exact subject. The imported design's phase exit requires an authenticated migration-audit approval whose gate_kind, request kind, request phase_instance, subject_digest equality with the approval, and explicit accept-import-audit decision all check out, plus an observed commit (src/state/transitions.ts:247-260); status derives migration_audit_required/accepted only from authenticated approvals carrying that same explicit decision. The composer additionally applies restart-eligibility filtering so it cannot disagree with advertised status after a planning restart. The new unrestorable-missing route does not bypass any gate: it reopens the produce window so a fresh terminal produce re-declares the drifted paths and the normal review/approval boundary covers the new bytes, and an already-open gate still takes precedence (src/state/next-action.ts:282-287). Local adoption creates no approval — it runs the existing initialization transaction over an artifact whose human authority is the earlier preview approval and the later migration-audit gate. Skill texts repeatedly forbid inferring authorization and require stopping when the server is unavailable (skills/archflow-prd/SKILL.md:16, skills/archflow-phase-impl/SKILL.md:16), and the status skill is pinned read-only with no archflow_apply call (skills/archflow-status/SKILL.md:8).
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: The change adds a migration-audit gate arm and a new import exit-authority path (src/state/request-composition.ts:614-623, src/state/status.ts:1160-1194, src/state/transitions.ts:247-260), adds a local adoption command, and changes recovery routing for missing projections (src/state/next-action.ts:288-317).

rule_findings.rationale: Failure and uncertainty stay visible with a safe next action. A missing recorded projection with no retained bytes is reported as exactly that, with an instruction naming the honest recovery rather than being silently adopted or ignored (src/state/next-action.ts:302-316); restorable cases keep the restore route, and unrelated mismatches still route to the human baseline-adoption gate. Server unavailability degrades to read-only manual-status and an explicit stop with no offline recording (skills across the set, e.g. skills/archflow-design/SKILL.md:16). The recorded host evidence is measured, not asserted: docs/validation/host-selection.json carries per-host advertisement, first-call selection, journey outcomes, and an observed_metrics block with an explicit blocked_journey_hosts counter, digest-bound to the shipped bundle manifest 79998d8d… which matches dist/manifest.json in this change set. The impl-notes report the earlier codex probe flake, the initially blocked Claude journey, and the skipped installs plainly instead of presenting a clean run. Minor: the notes cite claude 2.1.234 while the final artifact records 2.1.235, consistent with the re-recorded final run and not a misrepresentation of outcome.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: The change adds a degraded-path ladder to the status skill, a new non-success recovery route for unrestorable missing projections, and records real-host evidence under docs/validation/ including a run in which a host probe flaked.

rule_findings.rationale: Evidence stays bound to its own task and subject bytes, and mismatches fail closed. Adoption parses the task slug, resolves staging only under that task's workspace root, re-authenticates the staged manifest canonically, and refuses with CONTRACT_INVALID when the manifest task_id or import_digest disagrees with the staged descriptor, or with TASK_INVALID when state shows a different prior adoption (src/init/legacy-upgrade.ts:555-576); the deterministic adopt-legacy-import-<digest> intent makes retry a replay rather than a second effect. Migration-audit authority requires request.subject_digest === approval.subject_digest and a design-phase request before it can authorize the import exit. The absence-aware projection union resolves newest-per-path observations from this task's own retained manifests and retires declared deletions instead of carrying a stale cross-revision projection forward; adoption-sourced projections are marked unrestorable rather than treated as restorable evidence. Skill text explicitly forbids reading another task's files (skills/archflow-prd/SKILL.md:10).
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: The change adds a task-scoped local adoption command over staged import bytes (src/init/legacy-upgrade.ts:536-609), new subject-bound gate/exit authority, and reconciliation discovery over per-task retained manifests.
